title: PR drafting uses one local evidence pass and conservative validation claims

provenance.originSummary: Synthetic benchmark for the streamlined local PR drafting workflow.
provenance.whyItMattered: A PR drafting shortcut must preserve local branch accuracy and useful output without network refreshes, repository-wide auditing, or repeated fingerprints.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized runs cover direct Git branch authority, the ordinary two-batch local path, merge-aware and linear bounded stale-base recovery, complete local scope, targeted reads, conservative tests, in-memory schema conformance, and one cheap final stability guard.

description: A matrix covering the fast local evidence path, stale editor metadata, stale fork bases, authored tests versus executed tests, scope conflicts, and repository stability.

scope.notes: Each scenario is an independent no-network drafting invocation.

mustCatch.description: Without an explicit developer branch, direct Git from the validated current worktree owns the run and stale editor metadata cannot redirect discovery.
Repository identity and base candidates are collected in one fixed direct-Git batch, then merge base and complete change scope are collected in one fixed direct-Git batch.
Terminal calls contain only prompt-declared literal Git commands; file inspection and in-memory schema conformance do not generate PowerShell or shell programs.
Each prompt-declared Git batch is issued once in its canonical one-line semicolon form and is not first attempted with newlines or retried in alternate syntax.
One Phase 2 batch directly reads all selected material paths from the changed inventory without exact-path searches, test-function enumeration, service-directory listing, or staged evidence rounds.
The first usable upstream/main, origin/main, or local main ref is used without fetch or remote-tracking metadata changes.

A stale named main ref that inflates scope with incorporated provider history triggers one local first-parent metadata pass and one candidate scope pass; a strictly narrower coherent net scope continues drafting.

When contributor work surrounds a clear mainline integration merge, recovery uses the newest merge's second parent as its sole candidate and retains contributor changes from both sides without including incorporated mainline enhancements.
Recovery uses at most one candidate; an ambiguous boundary retains the original scope and leaves the later evidence-based intent classifier responsible for any hard stop.
Committed, staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked paths remain in one merge-base-to-working-tree inventory.
Primary implementation, registration, test, documentation, Resource Identity, List Resource, and security evidence is read concurrently only when applicable.
Changed matching tests can satisfy authored-test checklist items while test-passed items remain unchecked without explicit successful results.
One final HEAD and porcelain-status comparison hard-stops on change without hashing full content or restarting the workflow.
Two independent user-facing change intents with no dependency evidence stop drafting after material reads and before a title is guessed.
A shared helper and directly connected Resource consumers across service packages remain one coherent intent and continue drafting with every user-facing surface preserved.
Each terminal batch displays its exact command under a Read-only purpose label.
An ordinary run follows four primary phases with no more than 10 model iterations and 15 tool calls unless one concrete missing fact blocks an accurate draft.

mustNotFlag.description: The shortcut must not fetch or refresh remote-tracking refs.
The shortcut must not search GitHub for pull requests or potential issues.
The shortcut must not reload upstream contributor guides already represented by the checked-in contract.
The shortcut must not hash full staged, unstaged, and untracked contents twice or restart automatically.
A missing current worktree must request an explicit path rather than scanning roots or WSL distributions.
Test file presence alone must not check execution-dependent test claims.
Repository evidence must not use generated variables, loops, conditionals, script blocks, or fallback scripts.
The workflow must not reconstruct the template or serialize the draft payload into a terminal command for schema validation.
A fixed Git batch must not be attempted with newlines and then repeated with semicolons or another shell wrapper.
Phase 2 must not search for exact changed paths or enumerate test functions when changed paths already prove file ownership and authored coverage.
A coherent contributor feature must not hard-stop merely because a stale local main ref includes incorporated upstream commits in the initial scope.
Multiple service packages, paths, files, or Terraform surfaces alone must not trigger the unrelated-change hard stop.
Stale-base recovery must not fetch, query GitHub, inspect per-commit patches, test multiple candidate origins, or loop until a coherent scope appears.
An unrelated existing-Resource enhancement reachable only through the integrated mainline parent must not appear in the description, PR type, or changelog.
